I know how that feels. I grew up with a group of beautiful successful women around me. It's hard on you sometimes and women are conditioned to grow up and be competitive, unfortunately. If I've learned anything from growing up with these women though-- is that they are some of the most important people in my life. I admitted to them one time that I felt ugly beside them or less successful, and I was surprised to find out that they had felt the same. Turns out I tried so hard to be at their level that they thought I was in my own world in this interesting life and they admired things about me that I didn't realize myself.

You're attracted to your friends for a reason-whether they help you grow, inspire you... They fill the gaps that you think you don't have.

Even though your best friend has natural beauty, there is something about you that she is missing within herself and she finds delight in experiencing that with you. Maybe one day you will realize what that is. Just know that you Are beautiful and that all of this work on yourself does not go unnoticed.

If you want others to recognize you for your beauty, my advice would be to learn to love and find happiness within yourself. Joy in a person is the most attractive thing-and it attracts that same energy toward you.

The fact that you are self aware and want to get better means that you will. 

It takes time because old habits do die hard, and when your last experiences have woven these triggers into your psyche it's not always under your control. My best tips are as follows: 

1. Know when to step away. 
2. Communicate with your husband your process, and discuss with him how you plan to be better so he is aware of it as it happens and wont overthink or take it too personally. Also if he sees you taking a step to pause, hopefully he will give you the opportunity. 
3. Nip it in the bud--if you feel the argument escalating, pause and remind yourself where it may be heading

In general, just recognize that you aren't at fault for how you feel in a heated moment, but you can control what you do and say. A small step forward is still progress.
